title: Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
capsule: The double duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha was created by the territorial exchange settled at Hildburghausen in 1826, which reorganized the Ernestine Wettin sub-duchies after the Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg line died out, joining the Franconian duchy of Coburg to the Thuringian duchy of Gotha under a single ruler ruling each as a personal union. Duke Ernest I (r. 1826-1844) governed a state whose modest territory belied its rising dynastic weight: in the years immediately following its creation, the house leveraged marriage diplomacy to place its members on European thrones, most consequentially through Ernest's brother Leopold, who became the first King of the Belgians in 1831. By 1840 Ernest's younger son Albert married Queen Victoria of Britain, extending the dynasty's reach into the British royal line.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory is well defined from the 1826 treaty instruments and 19th-century German cadastral records; the dataset to=1840 reflects Prince Albert's departure for Britain rather than any territorial change, as the duchy continued until 1918.
